title: The Cold War: détente, renewed tension and the end (1963–1991)
summary: Vietnam and the Prague Spring, the rise and fall of détente, the 'Second Cold War' of the early 1980s and why the Cold War ended under Gorbachev.

keyterms.definition: Easing of Cold War tension in the late 1960s and 1970s through arms control, trade and summits.
1968 Soviet claim of the right to intervene in any socialist state where socialism was threatened, used to justify crushing the Prague Spring.
West German Chancellor Willy Brandt's policy of improving relations with East Germany and the Soviet bloc from 1969.
1972 Strategic Arms Limitation agreement freezing numbers of strategic missile launchers, signed with the ABM Treaty.
1975 agreement accepting Europe's post-war borders, with human-rights commitments later used by Eastern bloc dissidents.
Strategic Defense Initiative ('Star Wars'), Reagan's 1983 plan for a space-based missile shield.
'Openness': Gorbachev's policy allowing more freedom of speech and criticism.
'Restructuring': Gorbachev's attempt to reform the Soviet economy and political system.
1987 US–Soviet treaty eliminating all intermediate-range nuclear missiles, the first to abolish a whole class of weapons.
Nickname for Gorbachev's policy of letting Eastern European states choose their own path ('my way'), replacing the Brezhnev Doctrine.

questions.prompt: Who led the 1968 reform movement known as the Prague Spring?
questions.explanation: Dubček promised 'socialism with a human face'; Warsaw Pact forces invaded on 20–21 August 1968.

questions.text: The Soviet claim to intervene wherever socialism was threatened is the ___ Doctrine.
questions.explanation: It was announced after the invasion of Czechoslovakia.

questions.statement: President Nixon visited the People's Republic of China in February 1972.
questions.explanation: Exploiting the Sino-Soviet split, Nixon and Kissinger used 'triangular diplomacy' to pressure the USSR.

questions.prompt: Which factor encouraged the USA to seek détente around 1969–72?
options: The cost and unpopularity of the Vietnam War
questions.explanation: Vietnam strained the US economy and public support; the USSR had reached approximate nuclear parity.

questions.prompt: Match each agreement to its content.

pairs.right: Banned nuclear tests in the atmosphere
Aimed to stop the spread of nuclear weapons
Froze numbers of strategic missile launchers
Recognised borders and pledged human rights

questions.explanation: Arms control was the core of détente.

questions.prompt: Put these events in chronological order.

questions.text: Willy Brandt's policy of engagement with the East was called ___.
questions.explanation: It led to the 1972 Basic Treaty between the two German states.

questions.statement: The Helsinki Final Act's human-rights clauses ended up helping dissidents in the Eastern bloc.
questions.explanation: Groups such as Charter 77 in Czechoslovakia cited Helsinki commitments to criticise their governments.

questions.prompt: Which event is usually seen as ending détente?
options: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979
questions.explanation: Carter withdrew SALT II from the Senate, imposed a grain embargo and led a boycott of the 1980 Moscow Olympics.

options: The breakdown of relations between China and the USSR from the late 1950s
questions.explanation: Ideological and national rivalry led to Soviet advisers being withdrawn in 1960 and border clashes in 1969.

lessons.title: Second Cold War and the end (1979–1991)

questions.prompt: Which Reagan initiative alarmed Soviet leaders in 1983?
questions.explanation: SDI threatened to undermine deterrence and drew the USSR into an arms race it could not afford.
Glasnost allowed criticism that exposed the system's failures, such as the Chernobyl disaster (1986).

questions.prompt: Put these events in chronological order.
questions.explanation: March 1985, October 1986, December 1987, November 1989, December 1991.

questions.statement: The INF Treaty eliminated an entire category of nuclear weapons.
questions.explanation: It removed all US and Soviet ground-launched missiles with ranges of 500–5,500 km.

questions.prompt: Which explanation for the end of the Cold War emphasises internal Soviet problems?
options: Economic stagnation, the burden of Afghanistan and the arms race made reform unavoidable
Reagan's speeches alone forced Soviet surrender
questions.explanation: Historians debate the weight of Reagan's pressure, Gorbachev's choices and long-term Soviet decline.

questions.prompt: Match each person to their role.

pairs.right: Russian president who resisted the 1991 coup

questions.explanation: Pressure from below in Eastern Europe mattered alongside superpower diplomacy.

questions.text: Gorbachev's acceptance that Eastern European states could go their own way was nicknamed the ___ Doctrine.
questions.explanation: The refusal to use force allowed the revolutions of 1989 to succeed peacefully in most of the bloc.

questions.statement: Germany was reunified in October 1990, before the Soviet Union dissolved.
questions.explanation: Reunification took place on 3 October 1990; the USSR dissolved in December 1991.

questions.prompt: What was the effect of the failed August 1991 coup by Soviet hardliners?
options: It weakened Gorbachev, strengthened Yeltsin and sped up the collapse of the USSR
It led to a new Warsaw Pact
questions.explanation: Republics declared independence and Gorbachev resigned on 25 December 1991.

questions.prompt: When did Soviet forces complete their withdrawal from Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: Gorbachev called Afghanistan a 'bleeding wound'; the withdrawal signalled the end of Soviet expansionism.
